importance_ranking.reason: Buyers arrive with a defined area, crop type, and subsidy-compliance requirement — structure type, covering material, climate control, and frame specs are the primary shortlisting gate. A listing without these specs cannot be evaluated for NHB/MIDH eligibility or agronomic fit.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand with buyer recall at the structure level — market is fragmented across regional fabricators and empanelled vendors; buyers search by spec and subsidy eligibility, not manufacturer name (film brands like Ginegar are an exception but are a component, not the structure).
importance_ranking.reason: Subsidy-eligible buyers must procure from state horticulture department empanelled vendors — seller credentials (empanelment status, NHB/MIDH compliance track record, installation experience) are a hard eligibility gate, not a preference.

NHB/MIDH benchmark rates per sq. mt. are publicly known reference points; buyers compare listed rates against the benchmark to assess subsidy gap and seller competitiveness. Price varies substantially with structure type, covering material, and climate control tier — buyers discover and compare across spec tiers, making this spec-driven.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Turnkey projects may be quoted per project or per acre; material-only supply is quoted per kg/roll/piece. Per sq. mt. is the dominant and government-benchmarked unit for complete structures — must be shown to enable price comparison against NHB/MIDH rates.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared against NHB/MIDH benchmark rates without knowing the unit — per sq. mt. vs per project vs per acre creates real confusion for subsidy-driven buyers calculating their cost and subsidy gap.

Image helps buyers visually confirm structure type (NVPH vs tunnel vs dome) and construction quality, but specs and company credentials are the primary decision drivers. Absence of image reduces confidence but does not prevent shortlisting if specs are complete.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — Natural Ventilated vs Fan & Pad vs Fogging represents non-interchangeable tiers with 3–5x price difference and distinct agronomic suitability; a buyer cannot substitute one for another.

Polythene Film vs Polycarbonate Sheet vs Shade Net vs Insect Net drives significant price delta and determines crop protection capability — non-interchangeable across project requirements and subsidy eligibility criteria.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Buyers and NHB/MIDH subsidy calculations are always area-based — sellers need to know the installation area to quote accurately and confirm subsidy eligibility thresholds (minimum 500 sq. mt. for most schemes).

The majority of Indian polyhouse buyers are subsidy-driven — whether the structure meets NHB/MIDH technical standards (IS 1161 GI pipes, 200 micron UV film, HDG 275 GSM) is a primary purchase criterion that differentiates compliant from non-compliant offerings.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the product tier the buyer needs — Natural Vent vs Fan-Pad vs Fogger System are non-interchangeable and determine which sellers can supply; this single spec routes the RFQ to the correct supplier segment.
Installation area is the primary sizing and pricing variable — sellers cannot quote accurately or confirm subsidy eligibility without knowing the required coverage area.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires polythene film, polycarbonate sheet, shade net, or insect net to confirm product fit and quote the correct material cost — this is a primary price driver absent from the current buyer spec form.

Sellers who are NHB/MIDH empanelled vendors need to know upfront whether the buyer requires a subsidy-compliant structure — non-empanelled sellers cannot serve subsidy buyers, making this a hard routing signal.
